Exercise: Incline Dumbbell Flyes - With A Twist

Category:
strength

Exercise Type:
compound

Force Type:
push

Difficulty Level:
beginner

Movement Patterns:

- shoulder_abduction
- wrist_rotation

Primary Muscles:

- chest

Secondary Muscles:

- shoulders

Equipment:

- dumbbell

Fatigue Score:
2

Systemic Fatigue:
low

Stimulus To Fatigue Ratio:
0.8

Energy Requirement:
moderate

Recovery Time:
1 hours

Goals:

- shoulder_stability
- chest_strength

Contraindications:

- condition: shoulder instability, reason: The exercise may exacerbate existing shoulder issues due to the range of motion and wrist rotation involved.

Exercise Variations:

- name: Incline Dumbbell Flyes - With A Twist (Single Arm), instructions: ['Hold a dumbbell in one hand and lie on an incline bench that is set to an incline angle of no more than 30 degrees.', 'Extend the arm with a slight bend at the elbow.', 'Rotate the wrist so that the palm of your hand is facing you. Tip: The pinky fingers should be next to each other.', 'As you breathe in, start to slowly lower the arm to the side while keeping the arm extended and while rotating the wrist until the palm of the hand is facing the ceiling.', 'As you exhale start to bring the dumbbell back up to the starting position by reversing the motion and rotating the hand so that the pinky fingers are next to each other again. Tip: Keep in mind that the movement will only happen at the shoulder joint and at the wrist. There is no motion that happens at the elbow joint.', 'Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.']

Substitution Options:

- exercise_name: Incline Dumbbell Press, equipment: dumbbell

Instructions:

- Hold a dumbbell in each hand and lie on an incline bench that is set to an incline angle of no more than 30 degrees.
- Extend your arms above you with a slight bend at the elbows.
- Now rotate the wrists so that the palms of your hands are facing you. Tip: The pinky fingers should be next to each other. This will be your starting position.
- As you breathe in, start to slowly lower the arms to the side while keeping the arms extended and while rotating the wrists until the palms of the hand are facing each other. Tip: At the end of the movement the arms will be by your side with the palms facing the ceiling.
- As you exhale start to bring the dumbbells back up to the starting position by reversing the motion and rotating the hands so that the pinky fingers are next to each other again. Tip: Keep in mind that the movement will only happen at the shoulder joint and at the wrist. There is no motion that happens at the elbow joint.
- Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
